title: Machine copying joined fields
statement: For every alphabet $\Gamma$ and natural number $m$, there exist a finite state set, a deterministic Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with two work tapes, entry and exit states, and a constant $C$. For every input word, every list $f_s$ of $m$ fields, and every configuration $d$ in the entry state whose tape $0$ records the joined fields and whose tape $1$ is blank on the cells from one position before the record through its last position, the machine reaches its exit state at some time $t \le C(L+1)$, where $L$ is the length of the joined record. It does not visit the exit state earlier, every work-tape head stays within distance $C(L+1)$ of its initial position through time $t$, and at time $t$ tape $1$ contains the joined fields on the interval from its initial head position up to but excluding that position plus $L$; all other tape cells and the remaining configuration data are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An arbitrary alphabet $\Gamma$ and natural number $m$
The initial configuration is in the entry state
Tape $0$ records the joined fields on the specified interval
Tape $1$ is blank on the specified interval
The exit state is not reached before time $t$
All work-tape head displacements through time $t$ are at most $C(L+1)$
The final configuration has the specified tape-$1$ contents and otherwise preserves the configuration
